claim: ZFHX3 is necessary for the development of the SCN in mice
source: In the mouse, the transcription factor, ZFHX3 (zinc finger homeobox-3), is necessary for the development of the SCN and influences circadian behaviour in the adult.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to existing literature about ZFHX3's role in SCN development

claim: ZFHX3 influences circadian behaviour in adult mice
source: In the mouse, the transcription factor, ZFHX3 (zinc finger homeobox-3), is necessary for the development of the SCN and influences circadian behaviour in the adult.
evidence: This is supported by references to existing knowledge about ZFHX3 function

claim: A total of 43,236 ZFHX3-bound sites were found in the SCN genome
source: We found a total of 43,236 ZFHX3-bound sites, overlapping with approximately 22% of total modified histone regions in the SCN genome.
evidence: This is directly measured from ChIP-seq experimental data

claim: ZFHX3-bound sites overlap with approximately 22% of total modified histone regions in the SCN genome
source: We found a total of 43,236 ZFHX3-bound sites, overlapping with approximately 22% of total modified histone regions in the SCN genome.
evidence: This is calculated from ChIP-seq data comparing ZFHX3 binding with histone modifications

claim: About 60% of ZFHX3 bound sites were found near promoters (≤ 3 kb of transcription start sites)
source: About 60% of the ZFHX3 bound sites were found near promoters (≤ 3 kb of transcription start sites [TSS]) and so would be likely to identify direct transcriptional targets of ZFHX3
evidence: This is derived from analysis of ChIP-seq data showing genomic distribution of ZFHX3 binding

claim: About 21% of ZFHX3 bound sites were in distal intergenic regions
source: whilst ca. 21% were in distal intergenic regions potentially involved in other modes of gene regulation.
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data analysis of ZFHX3 binding locations

claim: 48.9% of total ZFHX3 peaks at ZT3 coincided with both H3K4me3 and H3K27ac occupancy
source: First, the majority of ZFHX3 peaks coincided with both H3K4me3 (trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 4) and H3K27ac (histone 3 lysine 27 acetylation) occupancy (48.9% of total ZFHX3 peaks at ZT3, Supplementary file 1)
evidence: This is quantified from ChIP-seq data comparing ZFHX3 with histone modification peaks

claim: ZFHX3 sites co-occupied with H3K4me3 and H3K27ac are focused near TSS (TSS ±3 kb)
source: First, the majority of ZFHX3 peaks coincided with both H3K4me3 (trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 4) and H3K27ac (histone 3 lysine 27 acetylation) occupancy (48.9% of total ZFHX3 peaks at ZT3, Supplementary file 1), and were focussed near TSS (TSS ±3 kb) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is shown in ChIP-seq data analysis and visualized in Figure 1B

claim: Sites with H3K4me3 and H3K27ac are likely responsible for active transcription
source: Since such sites are likely responsible for active transcription (Beacon et al., 2021), the ZFHX3 occupancy in these sites highlighted probable transcriptional regulation by ZFHX3 in the SCN.
evidence: This is based on cited literature (Beacon et al., 2021) about histone modification function

claim: ZFHX3 occupancy in sites with H3K4me3 and H3K27ac highlights probable transcriptional regulation by ZFHX3 in the SCN
source: Since such sites are likely responsible for active transcription (Beacon et al., 2021), the ZFHX3 occupancy in these sites highlighted probable transcriptional regulation by ZFHX3 in the SCN.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-localization of ZFHX3 with active transcription marks

claim: 20.7% of ZFHX3 sites were bound only by H3K4me3 (no H3K27ac)
source: Next, a subset of ZFHX3 sites (20.7%) were bound only by H3K4me3 (no H3K27ac) as illustrated at Figure 1C.
evidence: This is quantified from ChIP-seq data and shown in Figure 1C

claim: ZFHX3 sites bound only by H3K4me3 are indicative of poised transcriptional regulation
source: These are indicative of poised transcriptional regulation (Calo and Wysocka, 2013) and were also enriched near the TSS.
evidence: This is based on cited literature (Calo and Wysocka, 2013) about H3K4me3-only sites

claim: ZFHX3 sites bound only by H3K4me3 were enriched near the TSS
source: These are indicative of poised transcriptional regulation (Calo and Wysocka, 2013) and were also enriched near the TSS.
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: About 8.2% of ZFHX3 sites were bound by H3K27ac exclusively (no H3K4me3)
source: About 8.2% of ZFHX3 sites were bound by H3K27ac exclusively (no H3K4me3) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is quantified from ChIP-seq data and shown in Figure 1D

claim: ZFHX3 sites bound by H3K27ac exclusively were commonly found at intergenic and intronic regions
source: These sites were commonly found at intergenic and intronic regions and suggestive of enhancer-mediated gene regulation (Won et al., 2008).
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: ZFHX3 sites bound by H3K27ac exclusively are suggestive of enhancer-mediated gene regulation
source: These sites were commonly found at intergenic and intronic regions and suggestive of enhancer-mediated gene regulation (Won et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from cited literature (Won et al., 2008) about H3K27ac-only sites

claim: 22% of ZFHX3 sites were found to be devoid of modified histone binding
source: Finally, 22% of ZFHX3 sites were found to be devoid of modified histone binding and were also concentrated at distal intergenic regions (39.04%) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is quantified from ChIP-seq data and shown in Figure 1D

claim: ZFHX3 sites devoid of modified histone binding were concentrated at distal intergenic regions (39.04%)
source: Finally, 22% of ZFHX3 sites were found to be devoid of modified histone binding and were also concentrated at distal intergenic regions (39.04%) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data analysis and shown in Figure 1D

claim: ZFHX3 occupancy alongside histone modifiers near gene TSS and at distal intergenic regions suggests its crucial role in gene regulation potentially via promoter–enhancer interaction
source: Overall, the broad occurrence of ZFHX3 alongside histone modifiers near the gene TSS and at distal intergenic regions in the SCN genome suggests its crucial role in gene regulation potentially via promoter–enhancer interaction.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing ZFHX3 distribution patterns

claim: Genes associated with ZFHX3 and both H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone modifications are involved in neurodegeneration and axonal guidance
source: The functional annotation of genes which were associated with ZFHX3 and both the H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone modifications was found to be associated with neurodegeneration and axonal guidance, synaptic processes known to be important in the SCN (glutamatergic, GABAeric, and dopaminergic systems) and various signalling pathways.
evidence: This is derived from functional annotation analysis (DAVID) of genes near ZFHX3 binding sites

claim: Genes associated with ZFHX3 and both H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone modifications are involved in synaptic processes important in the SCN (glutamatergic, GABAeric, and dopaminergic systems)
source: The functional annotation of genes which were associated with ZFHX3 and both the H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone modifications was found to be associated with neurodegeneration and axonal guidance, synaptic processes known to be important in the SCN (glutamatergic, GABAeric, and dopaminergic systems) and various signalling pathways.
evidence: This is derived from functional annotation analysis of genes near ZFHX3 binding sites

claim: Genes associated with ZFHX3 and both H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone modifications include pathways involved with circadian entrainment and timekeeping
source: Importantly, they also included pathways involved with circadian entrainment and timekeeping (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), highlighting the reciprocal intersection between ZFHX3 and the SCN cell-autonomous clock.
evidence: This is shown in functional annotation analysis and visualized in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: Genomic regions cooperatively bound by ZFHX3 and H3K4me3 but with no H3K27ac are associated with genes involved in fundamental biological processes such as DNA replication or MAPK signalling, but not circadian rhythm
source: In contrast, genomic regions cooperatively bound by ZFHX3 and H3K4me3 but with no H3K27ac, or sites with ZFHX3 alone, were found to be associated with genes involved in several fundamental biological processes such as DNA replication or MAPK signalling, but notably not circadian rhythm (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is shown in functional annotation analysis and visualized in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: ZFHX3 binds at the TSS and regulates actively transcribing genes, particularly those involved in tissue-specific functions such as daily timekeeping
source: Therefore, it is plausible that ZFHX3 binds at the TSS and regulates actively transcribing genes, particularly those involved in tissue-specific functions such as daily timekeeping, while its occupancy without histone modifiers and/or at poised state regulates genes responsible for other basal functions.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq and functional annotation data

claim: ZFHX3 occupancy did not differ appreciably between ZT03 and ZT15 timepoints
source: Interestingly, it is worth noting that ZFHX3 occupancy did not differ appreciably between the two timepoints tested (ZT03 vs. ZT15): ZFHX3 was seen to bind consistently at the same genomic loci (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data comparing two timepoints

claim: ZFHX3 binds consistently at the same genomic loci across different timepoints
source: Interestingly, it is worth noting that ZFHX3 occupancy did not differ appreciably between the two timepoints tested (ZT03 vs. ZT15): ZFHX3 was seen to bind consistently at the same genomic loci (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is measured from ChIP-seq data

claim: Other factors/mechanisms confer temporal control to ZFHX3 binding sites whilst the presence of ZFHX3 is permissive to such cis- and trans-regulatory cues
source: This indicates that other factors/mechanisms confer temporal control to these sites whilst the presence of ZFHX3 is permissive to such cis- and trans-regulatory cues.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ZFHX3 binding does not change over time

claim: ZFHX3-bound sites revealed an over-representation of AT-rich motifs
source: We next examined the signature DNA binding motifs/cis-regulatory elements occupied by ZFHX3, either alone or with specific histone modifications (H3K4me3, H3K27ac). As anticipated, this revealed an over-representation of AT-rich motifs (Parsons et al., 2015).
evidence: This is measured from motif analysis (HOMER) of ChIP-seq data and consistent with cited literature

claim: ZFHX3-bound sites showed co-occurrence with SCN developmental and maintenance TFs such as DLX and LHX
source: Notably, it also suggested co-occurrence of ZFHX3 with SCN developmental and maintenance TFs such as DLX (distal-less homeobox) and LHX (LIM homeobox) (VanDunk et al., 2011) across the tested categories (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in motif analysis and visualized in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: ZFHX3-bound sites were enriched for RFX family of TFs, which have been implicated in transcriptional responses to light in the SCN
source: Furthermore, ZFHX3-bound sites were also enriched for non-AT-rich motifs such as the RFX family of TFs, which have been implicated in transcriptional responses to light in the SCN (Araki et al., 2004).
evidence: This is shown in motif analysis and supported by cited literature (Araki et al., 2004)

claim: ZFHX3 peaks adjacent to H3K27ac and H3K4me3 showed enrichment of ARNT (bHLH) domains
source: Interestingly, we noted enrichment of ARNT (bHLH) domains but only where ZFHX3 peaks were seen adjacent to H3K27ac and H3K4me3 (i.e., active promoters).
evidence: This is measured from motif analysis of ChIP-seq data

claim: The enrichment of ARNT domains at ZFHX3 sites points towards shared binding of ZFHX3 with circadian clock TFs BMAL1:CLOCK at E-boxes
source: This clearly points towards the possibility of shared binding of ZFHX3 with the circadian clock TFs BMAL1:CLOCK at E-boxes and highlights a point of interaction between the core TTFL and ZFHX3 in the regulation of circadian gene transcription in the central pacemaker.
evidence: This is inferred from the motif analysis showing ARNT enrichment at ZFHX3 sites

claim: The free-running circadian period was significantly shortened by conditional deletion of Zfhx3
source: Consistent with previous studies, this analysis showed that the free-running circadian period was significantly shortened by conditional deletion of Zfhx3 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is measured from behavioral wheel-running data and shown in Figure 2A

claim: The overall activity rhythm was less well defined with significantly reduced amplitude in Zfhx3-deleted mice
source: Furthermore, the overall activity rhythm was less well defined with significantly reduced amplitude, increased intra-daily variability and lower inter-daily stability in the deleted mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is measured from behavioral analysis and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D

claim: Zfhx3-deleted mice showed increased intra-daily variability in activity rhythm
source: Furthermore, the overall activity rhythm was less well defined with significantly reduced amplitude, increased intra-daily variability and lower inter-daily stability in the deleted mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is measured from behavioral analysis and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D

claim: Zfhx3-deleted mice showed lower inter-daily stability in activity rhythm
source: Furthermore, the overall activity rhythm was less well defined with significantly reduced amplitude, increased intra-daily variability and lower inter-daily stability in the deleted mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is measured from behavioral analysis and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D

claim: The loss of ZFHX3 compromised free-running circadian behaviour
source: The loss of ZFHX3 therefore compromised free-running circadian behaviour.
evidence: This is concluded from the behavioral data showing altered circadian parameters

claim: Animals with Zfhx3 gene deletion showed poor entrainment to the light cycle, with increased activity in the hours prior to the light to dark transition
source: Visual inspection of the actograms whilst the animals were in light/dark cycles suggested that animals with gene deletion showed poor entrainment to the light cycle, with animals showing increased activity in the hours prior to the light to dark transition (Figure 2A, right).
evidence: This is observed from actogram data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Gene-deleted animals showed a significant increase in wheel running activity in the hours prior to lights off (p<0.05 for ZT 10.5–12.5)
source: Pairwise analysis demonstrated that, compared to genetic control animals, gene-deleted animals showed a significant increase in wheel running activity in the hours prior to lights off (p<0.05 for ZT 10.5–12.5)
evidence: This is measured from statistical analysis of behavioral data

claim: Gene-deleted animals showed a significant reduction in wheel running activity in the hours prior to lights on (p<0.05 for ZT 20–23)
source: and a significant reduction in wheel running activity in the hours prior to lights on (p<0.05 for ZT 20–23).
evidence: This is measured from statistical analysis of behavioral data

claim: Gene-deleted animals showed an earlier onset of activity than controls
source: Consistent with this, analysis of the activity onset demonstrated that gene-deleted animals showed an earlier onset of activity than controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is measured from behavioral analysis and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E

claim: The phase advance under 12 h light/12 h dark in Zfhx3-deleted mice is consistent with the shortening of circadian period seen under DD
source: This phase advance under 12 h light/12 h dark is consistent with the shortening of circadian period seen under DD.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing behavioral data under different lighting conditions

claim: ZFHX3 contributes to circadian timekeeping and entrainment in the adult SCN, independently of any developmental roles
source: Thus, ZFHX3 contributes to circadian timekeeping and entrainment in the adult SCN, independently of any developmental roles.
evidence: This is concluded from the behavioral effects observed in adult-specific conditional knockout mice

claim: Almost 36% (n = 5637) of total assessed genes were affected by the acute loss of Zfhx3 in the SCN
source: As an initial analysis, we compared overall (i.e., time-independent) gene expression levels between the groups (Cre-neg vs. +Tamoxifen) to examine the global effect of Zfhx3 deletion on the SCN transcriptome and found that almost 36% (n = 5637) of total assessed genes were affected by the acute loss of Zfhx3 in the SCN.
evidence: This is measured from RNA-seq differential expression analysis

claim: 2725 genes were downregulated in +Tamoxifen animals compared to Cre-neg controls
source: Of these, 2725 were downregulated and 2912 upregulated in +Tamoxifen animals compared to Cre-neg controls. (Supplementary file 3, Figure 3A).
evidence: This is measured from RNA-seq differential expression analysis and shown in Figure 3A

claim: 2912 genes were upregulated in +Tamoxifen animals compared to Cre-neg controls
source: Of these, 2725 were downregulated and 2912 upregulated in +Tamoxifen animals compared to Cre-neg controls. (Supplementary file 3, Figure 3A).
evidence: This is measured from RNA-seq differential expression analysis and shown in Figure 3A

claim: Both control groups (Cre-neg and -Tamoxifen) showed consistent differential gene expression levels compared to the mutant
source: Furthermore, as expected, both the control groups (Cre-neg and -Tamoxifen) showed consistent differential gene expression levels compared to the mutant which mitigated any potential downstream effect of tamoxifen dosing per se (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is shown in RNA-seq data comparison and visualized in Figure 3B and C

claim: 80% (n = 4543) of total differentially expressed genes revealed ZFHX3 occupancy at their promoter sites along with histone modifications (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac)
source: Of the total differentially expressed genes, 80% (n = 4543) revealed ZFHX3 occupancy at their promoter sites along with histone modifications (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac), showing a direct interaction between ZFHX3 bound TSS (±3 kb) and gene expression (p=0, OR = 6.3, Jaccard index = 0.4, signifying strong association).

claim: There is a direct interaction between ZFHX3 bound TSS (±3 kb) and gene expression (p=0, OR = 6.3, Jaccard index = 0.4, signifying strong association)
source: Of the total differentially expressed genes, 80% (n = 4543) revealed ZFHX3 occupancy at their promoter sites along with histone modifications (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac), showing a direct interaction between ZFHX3 bound TSS (±3 kb) and gene expression (p=0, OR = 6.3, Jaccard index = 0.4, signifying strong association).

claim: Only 7% of differentially expressed genes (n = 381) were solely bound by ZFHX3 at the TSS (p=0.37, OR = 1, Jaccard index = 0.1, signifying weak association)

claim: The effect of ZFHX3 on gene transcription is predominantly observed when jointly occupied by histone modification at gene TSS

claim: Genes that were downregulated after Zfhx3 deletion are associated with circadian rhythm
source: Consistent with previous studies (Hughes et al., 2021; Parsons et al., 2015; Wilcox et al., 2021; Wilcox et al., 2017), genes that were downregulated were seen to be associated with neuropeptide signalling pathways (Vip, Grp), circadian rhythm, neuron differentiation etc.
